title: ZnO/ZIF-8@Au nanoarchitectures with nanoconfinement-enhanced plasmonic coupling for ultrasensitive photoelectrochemical detection of malondialdehyde.
abstract: Malondialdehyde (MDA) is a pivotal oxidative stress biomarker implicated in cardiovascular diseases, neurodegeneration, and cancer; however, its trace quantification in complex biological matrices remains analytically daunting. Photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensing offers inherently low background noise and exceptional sensitivity for trace bioanalysis. Nevertheless, efficiently translating molecular recognition into amplified PEC signals remains a challenge. We report a nanoconfinement-mediated PEC interface that integrates covalent molecular conjugation with plasmonic amplification within a crystalline matrix scaffold. Within this nanoconfined environment, localized Au nanoparticles serve as plasmonic amplifiers that anchor 4-aminothiophenol (4-ATP) receptors. Upon MDA recognition, the optimized sensor exhibits dual linear detection ranges spanning 0.001 to 1.0 nmol L-1 (R12 = 0.9928) and 1.0 to 1000 nmol L-1 (R22 = 0.9992), yielding an ultralow detection limit of 0.3 pmol L-1. The confined Schiff-base reaction between 4-ATP and MDA generates an interfacial reaction product, leading to a new absorption band at approximately 450 nm and modulation of the Au LSPR band. This change is mainly attributed to the altered local dielectric environment around Au NPs. Wavelength-dependent operando transient photovoltage spectroscopy (TPV) provides mechanistic evidence that plasmon-driven hot-carrier injection augments PEC signal output. Overall, this work establishes an interface-engineering paradigm that integrates molecular conjugation with plasmonic coupling, offering a promising blueprint for the PEC detection of small-molecule biomarkers.

title: Plant-wearable fluorescent hydrogel patch based on PDA-PEI copolymer dots for on-site visual detection of glyphosate.
abstract: Glyphosate (GLY) residues are difficult to remove from agricultural products and pose potential risks to food safety, making their sensitive detection highly desirable. In this study, a Cu2+-mediated ratiometric fluorescence sensing platform was constructed for the sensitive detection of GLY by physically mixing polydopamine-polyethyleneimine copolymer dots (PDA-PEI CPDs) with terephthalic acid (PTA) based on a competitive coordination strategy. Cu2+ coordinated with the amino groups on the surface of CPDs and the carboxyl groups of PTA to form a CPDs-PTA-Cu2+ complex. This process quenched the green fluorescence of CPDs at 530 nm while generating a new blue emission at 450 nm. Upon the addition of GLY, competitive coordination between GLY and Cu2+ disrupted the complex, resulting in fluorescence recovery at 530 nm and fluorescence quenching at 450 nm, thereby producing a ratiometric fluorescence response. The sensor shows linear ranges of 0-80 μg/mL for GLY (LOD = 5.73 ng/mL). To meet the requirements of on-site applications, a CPDs-Cu2+@sodium alginate hydrogel was further prepared. Under 365 nm excitation, the hydrogel responded to GLY through single-emission fluorescence recovery at 530 nm. The hydrogel enabled smartphone-assisted RGB quantitative analysis and in situ semi-quantitative screening of GLY on vegetable surfaces using a wearable hydrogel patch. By integrating solution-phase ratiometric fluorescence quantification with hydrogel-based visual readout, a simple and portable sensing platform was established for accurate GLY determination and visual screening of surface residues.

title: Signal-amplified electrochemical aptasensor based on multi-branched circular DNA and bimetallic nanomaterials for sensitive histamine detection in complex food matrices.
abstract: Histamine is a high-risk biogenic amine produced during food spoilage. Excessive intake can trigger severe allergic reactions or poisoning, making the development of an accurate detection method critically important. This study proposes a novel electrochemical aptasensor for the sensitive detection of histamine. The sensor comprises a multi-branched circular DNA structure, thionine/Au@prussian blue analog (Thi/Au@PBA), Au@Pd nanoflowers (Au@Pd NFs), and an Apt screened via molecular docking and experiment. Compared with the linear DNA, the amplification effect of the circular was observed with low and high concentrations, demonstrating that the circular structure can effectively enhance the sensor's signal. The response signal difference between the presence and absence of the target on the Au@Pd NFs-modified electrode was 1.55 times that of the bare electrode. Furthermore, in a solution of Thi at a certain concentration, the signal response of the Au@PBA-modified electrode was 2.77 times that of the bare electrode. The resulting aptasensor exhibited an ultra-low detection limit of 2.16 pg/mL and a broad linear range (0.01-500 ng/mL) for histamine, alongside high selectivity, reproducibility, repeatability and stability. The sensor's accurate detection results in food matrices (salmon, canned tuna, and red wine) have confirmed its practical value. This study proposes an electrochemical aptasensor based on multi-branched circular DNA and bimetallic nanomaterials for the sensitive detection of histamine. This sensor shows great potential in the field of rapid food safety detection.

title: Central Neuroendocrine Governance as a Unifying Framework for Host-Tumor Interaction: From Afferent Sensing to Therapeutic Modulation.
abstract: Cancer is not biologically confined to the tumor bed. Cachexia, fatigue, metabolic dysfunction, circadian disruption, and immune dysfunction reflect disturbances that local models alone cannot fully explain. The brain is well positioned to participate in these processes because it continuously samples circulating signals and coordinates endocrine and autonomic responses. Yet the afferent side of this communication has received less attention than its downstream consequences. Here, we synthesize evidence showing that cytokines, hormones, metabolites, and cargo carried by extracellular vesicles can engage central sensory interfaces and integrative regions, particularly circumventricular organs and hypothalamic and brainstem circuits. We use the term Endocriception to describe afferent humoral sensing and early central decoding of circulating biochemical signals, and focus here on how tumor- and host-associated changes engage this process in cancer. Central neuroendocrine governance refers to the subsequent integration of this information and the generation of autonomic and endocrine outputs. Persistent inflammation, stress, circadian disruption, and impaired feedback may gradually reconfigure this regulatory system. The resulting changes can affect systemic immunity, metabolism, behavior, and host tolerance of cancer. Evidence is strongest for a limited number of pathways, whereas many proposed links remain incomplete or dependent on tumor type and experimental context. We therefore present central neuroendocrine governance as a working framework for organizing current evidence and guiding mechanistic studies, biomarker development, and interventions aimed at restoring host physiology.

title: Decoding Spatial Attention in the Cocktail Party Problem Using Whole-head High-Density fNIRS.
abstract: Spatial attention is critical for solving the cocktail party problem, a longstanding problem in neuroscience and artificial speech recognition. The ability to decode where humans are attending in a cocktail party like scene would empower applications in brain computer interfaces and assistive devices such as hearing aids. Here we demonstrate that, in an overt attention task, the attended spatial location can be decoded robustly from single trial hemodynamic responses, using a whole head high density fNIRS system. We also identify critical brain regions that make the highest contribution to decoding accuracy. Specifically, we find that decoding based on a small fraction of channels located within the left and right inferior parietal lobule (IPL) achieves maximal decoding accuracy comparable to all channels. Decoding fell close to chance in a covert auditory condition in which participants held central fixation while attending to the same talkers, indicating that auditory attention alone without orientation is not sufficient for decoding. Finally, control experiments suggest that overt-condition decoding is influenced by sustained eye position/gaze direction, not eye movement. These results support the development of fNIRS-integrated BCIs and assistive devices controlled by overt spatial attention.

title: Ziziphora clinopodioides Flavonoids exerts neuroprotective effects through PI3K/Akt pathway to improve ischemic stroke.
abstract: Ziziphora clinopodioides Lam. is a traditional Uyghur medicinal herb used for centuries in Xinjiang, China, to treat cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disorders. According to local ethnopharmacological records, it is traditionally employed to promote blood circulation, remove blood stasis, calm the heart, and relieve chest tightness and palpitations. Modern studies have shown that its total flavonoids (ZCF) possess anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. Ischemic stroke (IS) is a leading cause of death and disability, involving neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption. However, the neuroprotective mechanism of ZCF against IS and its active constituents remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the neuroprotective mechanism of ZCF against IS and to identify its potential active flavonoids. Network pharmacology and transcriptomics were used to predict core pathways, followed by in vitro and in vivo experiments. Neurological deficits, infarct volume, BBB integrity, and PI3K/Akt-related inflammatory/oxidative markers were assessed. The PI3K inhibitor LY294002 was used, and active flavonoids were screened by molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and ELISA. Integrated transcriptomics and network pharmacology identified that ZCF modulates the PI3K/Akt pathway. In MCAO/R-treated rats, ZCF reduced cerebral infarction, and preserved neuronal morphology. ZCF protected BBB integrity by restoring ZO-1, Occludin, Claudin-5, reducing MMP-9 and MMP-2 levels, rebalancing the Ang-1/Ang-2 ratio, decreasing NaF permeability, and increasing TEER. ZCF activated PI3K/Akt signaling in both bEnd.3 cells and MCAO/R-treated rat brain tissues, and the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 reversed ZCF-mediated regulation of tight junction proteins, matrix metalloproteinases, and Ang-1/Ang-2, suggesting that ZCF preserves BBB integrity at least partly through a PI3K/Akt-dependent mechanism. ZCF inhibited the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 axis, reduced IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α and MDA, and up-regulated Nrf2 and SOD, and these effects were reversed by LY294002. Molecular docking and MD simulations suggested that Diosmin, Glycitin, and Tilianin may form stable binding with PI3K. Diosmin, Glycitin and Tilianin could significantly restore the activity of PI3K in PC12 cells treated with OGD/R, reduce the levels of IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α and MDA, and enhance the activity of SOD. Under preconditioning conditions, ZCF maintains BBB and inhibits neuroinflammation and oxidative stress through integrity and PI3K/Akt dependence, thereby exerting anti-IS protection. Diosmin, Glycitin, and Tilianin are potential active flavonoids that may contribute to PI3K/Akt activation.

title: Aberrant amygdala subregion volumes in youth at high risk for bipolar disorder predict antidepressant-induced adverse events.
abstract: Youth with familial risk for bipolar disorder (BD) and current depression/anxiety are vulnerable to antidepressant-induced adverse events (AE), including mania. The amygdala, implicated in the pathophysiology of mood disorders, may play a key role in these AE. 105 youth with at least one first-degree relative with BD-I and a current depressive/anxiety disorder (high-risk) and 51 healthy controls (HC) underwent baseline MRI to investigate neurostructural risk factors for antidepressant-induced AE. High-risk youth were randomized to either psychotherapy plus escitalopram or psychotherapy plus placebo (2:1) for up to 16 weeks. Clinical efficacy was assessed using the Children's Depression Rating Scale-Revised and Pediatric Anxiety Rating Scale, and AE were assessed using the Pediatric Adverse Events Rating Scale and Treatment-Emergent Activation and Suicidality Assessment Profile. Baseline amygdala subregion volumes and their associations with the rates of change in clinical symptoms and AE over time were evaluated using linear regression models. Compared to HC, high-risk youth had reduced volumes in left lateral and medial nuclei, bilateral central and cortical nuclei, and bilateral corticoamygdaloid transition area and increased volumes in bilateral basal and accessory basal nuclei. In escitalopram-treated youth, but not those receiving placebo, smaller baseline volumes in bilateral cortical nuclei and left medial nucleus were associated with fewer arousal-related AE. Additionally, larger bilateral basal nuclei volumes at baseline were associated with more arousal-related AE. Widespread amygdala volume abnormalities provide insights into neurobiological mechanisms underlying the development of BD in high-risk youth, and specific subregion volumes may serve as neurostructural markers for predicting antidepressant-induced AE.

title: Longitudinal wearable monitoring and polygenic score for major depressive disorder in the All of Us Research Program.
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) susceptibility reflects both stable inherited liability and dynamic behavioral patterns, yet these dimensions are rarely examined together using long-term data in real-world settings. Here, we integrated genomic, electronic health record (EHR), and longitudinal Fitbit wearable data from 3030 adults of genetically inferred European ancestry in the All of Us Research Program, 284 of whom had an EHR-recorded MDD diagnosis during follow-up after a 180-day baseline period. Time-varying Cox models examined associations of the MDD polygenic score (PGS), monthly wearable-derived physical activity and sleep features, and wearable feature × MDD PGS interactions with EHR-recorded MDD. Higher MDD PGS, lower daily steps, lower light and vigorous physical activity, lower sleep efficiency, and greater sleep duration variability were associated with a higher hazard of EHR-recorded MDD. The associations of sedentary time and sleep duration variability with MDD differed across MDD PGS levels, with stronger associations among participants with higher MDD PGS. Model-estimated hazard ratio curves across MDD PGS levels further showed that the behavioral levels corresponding to the same relative hazard differed across levels of genetic liability, with more favorable behavioral levels observed at higher MDD PGS levels. Sequentially integrating MDD PGS, baseline wearable features, monthly wearable features, and selected wearable feature × MDD PGS interactions increased model discrimination, with the C-index increasing from 0.637 to 0.705. These findings support the complementary value of genetic liability and longitudinal behavioral monitoring for characterization of MDD susceptibility and may inform work on genetically informed digital phenotyping for personalized monitoring and prevention.

title: Overcoming drug delivery barriers to Unlock the therapeutic potential of conventional chemotherapy in glioblastoma.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains one of the most incurable malignancies, and systemic therapies continue to provide only limited clinical benefit despite encouraging preclinical evidence. Therapeutic failure has traditionally been attributed to insufficient drug efficacy or intrinsic resistance mechanisms. However, increasing evidence suggests that many conventional chemotherapeutic agents retain substantial antitumor activity but fail to achieve sufficient intratumoral exposure because of delivery barriers. This review proposes that inadequate drug delivery represents a major barrier limiting the therapeutic efficacy of conventional chemotherapeutics in GBM, independent of their intrinsic pharmacodynamic activity. We re-evaluate conventional chemotherapeutic agents, including alkylating agents, microtubule-targeting agents, topoisomerase inhibitors, and platinum compounds, from the perspective of blood-brain barrier (BBB) transport, heterogeneous intratumoral drug distribution, and dose-limiting systemic toxicity. We further discuss how emerging drug delivery strategies can restore the therapeutic potential of these agents by improving brain penetration and intratumoral distribution without altering their intrinsic pharmacological properties.By reframing chemotherapy failure in GBM as a consequence of both pharmacodynamic resistance and inadequate drug delivery, this Review highlights drug delivery as an underappreciated determinant of therapeutic efficacy.

title: Implementation rules and research status of acupuncture therapy for anxiety disorders.
abstract: In recent years, the number of studies on acupuncture intervention for anxiety disorders has been gradually increasing, and its application scope in clinical practice has also been expanding. This article intends to review and discuss the combination of common acupoints, specific operation methods, efficacy evaluation indicators, clinical effects and potential mechanisms of action. Available evidence suggests that acupuncture may influence anxiety-related symptoms through multiple neurobiological pathways, including autonomic regulation, neurotransmitter signaling, neuroendocrine regulation, and neuroplasticity-related mechanisms; however, the causal contribution of individual pathways remains incompletely established. However, there are still some shortcomings in relevant studies, such as limited sample size, lack of uniformity in efficacy criteria, and relatively insufficient follow-up time. Future research should pay more attention to the application of evidence-based medicine methods, strengthen the discussion of mechanisms of action, and try to establish more individualized intervention plans.

title: Neurodegenerative diseases in Sub-Saharan Africa: diagnostic invisibility, biological heterogeneity and a precision-neuroscience agenda.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) are increasingly recognised in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), but the principal scientific challenge is no longer simply to document a presumed hidden burden. It is to determine how much of the observed heterogeneity reflects underlying neurobiology and how much arises from age structure, case ascertainment, culturally sensitive phenotyping and unequal access to neurological diagnosis. This critical narrative review synthesises evidence from 2000 to July 2026 across epidemiology, disease mechanisms, genomics, biomarkers, environmental exposures, therapeutics and health systems, using Tanzania as an illustrative case rather than a regional proxy. Community studies demonstrate substantial diagnostic invisibility, while recent African-ancestry research shows that inclusion of genetically diverse populations can reveal mechanisms that are poorly captured in ancestry-restricted datasets. The glucosylceramidase beta 1 (GBA1) rs3115534-G Parkinson's disease signal provides a proof of principle, linking an African-ancestry-enriched association to altered ribonucleic acid (RNA) splicing and glucocerebrosidase biology. Emerging plasma biomarkers and ancestry-aware genomics create a route from syndromic diagnosis towards biological characterisation, but thresholds and models require population-specific validation. This review proposes that the next phase of African neurodegeneration research should integrate culturally valid phenotype, biomarkers, imaging, genomics, measured exposures and longitudinal outcomes from inception. Such platforms could distinguish measurement artefact from biological variation, improve regional diagnosis and test the global generalisability of prevailing models of neurodegeneration.

title: Propofol suppresses intrinsic excitability and alters excitatory synaptic plasticity in ventral tegmental area dopamine neurons.
abstract: Propofol (2,6-diisopropylphenol) is a short-acting intravenous anesthetic used to induce and maintain general anesthesia. Beyond its anesthetic actions, propofol can produce rewarding subjective effects and has abuse potential. Because ventral tegmental area (VTA) dopamine neurons contribute to reward processing and arousal, we examined the effects of propofol on their intrinsic and excitatory synaptic properties using whole-cell patch-clamp recordings in acute rat midbrain slices. At 100 μM, propofol reduced evoked action-potential firing and increased rheobase in putative VTA dopamine neurons. It also reduced the AMPA/NMDA ratio of glutamatergic synaptic currents. A spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) protocol induced sustained long-term potentiation (LTP) under control conditions, whereas the same protocol in the presence of 100 μM propofol produced persistent LTD-like synaptic depression. These findings show that, under acute slice conditions, propofol alters intrinsic excitability, excitatory synaptic balance, and activity-dependent synaptic plasticity in putative VTA dopamine neurons. Whether these cellular effects contribute to propofol-related arousal or reward behaviors remains to be tested.

title: Neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease: From glial cell states and molecular networks to biomarkers and precision therapeutics.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is now recognized as a biologically heterogeneous syndrome in which amyloid-β pathology, Tau-related alterations, and neuroinflammation are key interconnected processes. Microglia, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, complement, inflammasomes, neurovascular cells, and peripheral immunity are implicated as both adaptive and disease-promoting contributors to the pathophysiology of AD. Here, we highlight mechanisms by which innate immunity and peripheral immune cells influence amyloid β-peptide metabolism, Tau pathophysiology, excitatory synaptic function, oxidative stress response, blood-brain barrier integrity, and systemic inflammation in the context of Alzheimer's disease. A particular focus is made on the role of TREM2-related microglial function and the NLRP3 inflammasome, complement-mediated synaptic pruning, astrocyte crosstalk, and the limitations of the M1/M2 and A1/A2 concepts. A distinction is made between biomarkers of core AD pathophysiology and those specific to neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration. An emphasis is placed on the clinical utility of plasma p-tau217 in combination with Aβ42/Aβ40, GFAP, NfL, sTREM2, YKL-40, and neuroinflammation imaging. With respect to therapeutics, an effort is made to focus on the need to harness desirable inflammatory pathways while specifically targeting deleterious processes rather than adopting an overarching anti-inflammatory approach. Single-cell, spatial, multi-omics, and biomarker-driven approaches may enable patient stratification based on underlying pathophysiology, allowing for stage-specific combination therapeutic strategies. Overall, studies presented in this review highlight a precision-neuroimmunology concept in which neuroinflammatory processes are both triggers and effectors of disease pathology and can be selectively modulated for clinical benefit.

title: Translational Evaluation of In Vitro-to-In Vivo Extrapolation Techniques for Brain Penetration Using Open Flow Microperfusion and Microdialysis in Rats.
journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
abstract: There is a growing need to leverage mathematical models of the central nervous system (CNS) with translational approaches employing in vitro-in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) approaches. As a benchmark of brain penetration, unbound brain partitioning (Kp,uu), and subsequently a combination of cerebral Open Flow Microperfusion (cOFM) and microdialysis (MD) were evaluated in rats. Additionally, a six-compartment physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model of the CNS was developed in rats using six drugs with varying affinities to the P-glycoprotein (P-gp) transporter to learn and verify the in vivo studies. Active and passive drug efflux and permeability parameters derived from two P-gp overexpressing cell lines (MDCK-I and LLC-PK1) were scaled using proteomics-informed methods. Model predictions were evaluated with data obtained from terminal brain-to-plasma partition coefficient from both rat cOFM and MD experiments. In correcting for loss of drug in both the cOFM and MD equipment, a relative recovery (RR) showed significantly higher recovery in cOFM compared to MD experiments; for phenytoin, quinidine, and verapamil these were 0.53/0.063, 0.73/0.46, and 0.16/0.04 (cOFM/MD), respectively. Notably, higher P-gp efflux obtained from experiments with MDCK-I-transfected cells resulted in simulated lower drug concentrations in brain compartments. Overall, the CNS-IVIVE-PBPK model tended to overpredict brain drug concentrations, especially using data obtained from transfected LLC-PK1 cells. However, there is better agreement between the model predictions and the observed data for whole-brain concentrations obtained from terminal studies. We also demonstrated the feasibility of an IVIVE framework that integrates cell line derived passive and active drug parameters to estimate brain concentrations.

title: Neuroprotective potential of safinamide against LPS-induced neuroinflammation and cognitive dysfunction in mice.
abstract: Neuroinflammation, a key pathological hallmark of neurological diseases, contributes to neurodegeneration, synaptic dysfunction, and cognitive decline. Safinamide shows toll-like receptor-mediated anti-inflammatory effects in cellular models; however, it's in vivo neuroprotective and neuroinflammatory effects remain unexplored. In the present investigation, the anti-neuroinflammatory impact of safinamide was evaluated in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced mice using behavioral, biochemical, and histopathological assessments. LPS was administered intraperitoneally from days 8 to 15 to induce neuroinflammation, followed by 15 days of safinamide treatment at 10 mg/kg and 20 mg/kg. Safinamide 20 mg/kg significantly improved spatial and recognition memory, as evidenced by the percentage alternation in the Y-maze and recognition index in the novel object recognition test. Furthermore, safinamide significantly reduced the levels of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), phosphorylated NF-κB (p-NF-κB), NLRP3, TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, acetylcholinesterase (AChE), and malondialdehyde (MDA), and increased levels of glutathione (GSH), catalase, and superoxide dismutase (SOD). Histopathological analysis revealed decreased amyloid-β deposition and preservation of neuronal architecture. These findings suggest that safinamide modulates neuroinflammatory and oxidative stress pathways and exhibits promising neuroprotective potential against inflammation-associated cognitive impairment.

title: Temporal misalignment of brain-heart coupling accounts for multilevel interoceptive dysfunction in schizophrenia.
abstract: Schizophrenia involves profound disturbances in the sense of a bodily self. These disturbances increasingly appear to arise from disrupted interoception, the perception of internal physiological signals. However, dominant models that emphasize either intrinsic neural timescales or interoceptive inference tend to treat cardiac signals merely as passive sensory inputs. Here, we propose that cardiac rhythm dynamics may provide a phase-based temporal reference for large-scale neural coordination, potentially synchronizing neural activity across otherwise disparate temporal scales. This scaffolding function is mediated by mechanically transduced pulsatile signals that may influence cortical excitability across distributed networks. Within this framework, interoceptive dysregulation in schizophrenia is reconceptualized as a decoupling of hierarchical cortical oscillations from peripheral cardiac phases. Reduced variability in cardiac rhythms may weaken the stability of temporal references available to higher-order networks. This, in turn, may drive a compensatory increase in the prior precision assigned to ambiguous visceral inputs, thereby increasing ambiguity in distinguishing internally generated from externally driven signals. Such processes may contribute to hallucinations, delusions, and motivational deficits. Emerging therapeutic strategies, therefore, aim to restore temporal alignment across the heart-brain axis. Translating the phenomenology of interoception into quantifiable metrics of neuro-visceral misalignment holds promise as a potential bridge between neurobiology and targeted psychiatric intervention.

title: Neuronal progranulin in the medial prefrontal cortex mediates stress-induced despair-like behaviors and impaired neuroplasticity.
abstract: Neuroplasticity in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) is critically implicated in major depressive disorder (MDD). Progranulin (PGRN), a multifunctional protein that is abundant in the cortex, regulates neuronal development and synaptic maintenance, positioning it as a candidate therapeutic target for MDD. However, current findings indicate the effects of PGRN in depression are contingent upon both brain region and cell type. Whether neuronal PGRN in the mPFC contributes to the pathogenesis of depression remains unknown. A chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mouse model was established, followed by depression-related behavioral tests. PGRN expression levels were determined by western blotting and immunofluorescence. Adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated neuronal Grn knockdown was performed in the mPFC in vivo to assess the functional contribution of PGRN. Neuronal morphology was evaluated by Golgi staining and Sholl analysis. Transcriptional changes were profiled by RNA sequencing to explore potential mechanisms, with bioinformatics analyses including differentially expressed genes (DEGs), Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG), gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis. PGRN expression was increased in mPFC neurons after CUMS exposure. Neuronal Grn knockdown in the mPFC partially reversed CUMS-induced despair-like behaviors and impaired dendritic plasticity. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed that Grn knockdown restored CUMS-induced neuroplasticity-related transcriptional alterations, including genes involved in Ephrin signaling, planar cell polarity, and MYC-related transcriptional programs. These findings suggest that neuronal PGRN in the mPFC contributes to the despair-like phenotype, likely through modulation of neuroplasticity. Targeting neuronal PGRN may represent a potential strategy for developing novel antidepressant interventions.

title: Proteinopathies and glial cells.
An Efficient Convolutional Neural Network Model for Classifying Positive Affective States from EEG Data Considering Sleep Condition.
abstract: The recognition of affective states from EEG recordings considering the sleep condition can be an important supporting tool in therapy and in the treatment of psychological or psychiatric disorders. Since sleep deprivation changes EEG characteristics, a two-stage framework is developed for affective state classification. First, a classification between "Normal Sleep" (NS) and "Sleep-Deprived" (SD) is conducted using resting-state EEG data. The data are then fed into one of two newly proposed, lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to recognize four affective states. In the first stage, CNN-BiLSTM achieves 95.96% accuracy under window-level splitting and 70.46% under subject-independent 5-fold cross-validation, while in the second stage the proposed models achieve 93.40% (NS) and 90.95% (SD) under window-level splitting, and 38.98% (NS) and 38.97% (SD) under cross-validation. The lower subject-independent accuracies reflect the class imbalance and the clustering of scores near the class boundaries, which make cross-subject four-class generalization challenging. As existing studies mostly classify momentary emotions without addressing sleep conditions, direct comparison with prior work is difficult; we therefore benchmarked our framework against several established baseline models, including SqueezeNet, EEGNet, ShallowConvNet, Support Vector Machine, and Random Forest. This study suggests that considering physiological states can improve multi-class classification of affective states from time-varying neurophysiological signals such as EEG. The framework performs strongly under window-level evaluation, whereas its performance under the stricter subject-independent setting is more limited and should be interpreted accordingly. It can nonetheless contribute to more comprehensive research in affective neuroscience.

title: Use of the arousal-based individual screening model for studying post-traumatic stress disorder: findings and future directions.
abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a debilitating psychiatric condition arising in a subset of trauma-exposed susceptible individuals, yet the pathophysiological determinants of this individual variability remain largely unresolved. We developed the arousal-based individual screening (AIS) model with the aim of filling key gaps in the preclinical field. The AIS model identifies susceptible and resilient mice of both sexes by applying z-normalization of post-trauma changes in acoustic startle reactivity (ASR) induced by a single 24-hour restraint. Susceptible mice develop a long-lasting, multi-domain PTSD-like phenotype with behavioral abnormalities persisting for at least 75 days post-trauma. Critically, trauma susceptibility rates are sex-dependent: approximately 25-35% in males and 35-45% in females, recapitulating clinically observed sex differences in PTSD prevalence. The AIS model shows face, construct, and predictive validity, including pharmacological response to chronic paroxetine in susceptible animals. Since its establishment, we have used the AIS model to investigate three major pathophysiological dimensions of PTSD susceptibility: epigenetic regulation via brain-region-specific miRNA dysregulation; gut-brain axis dysfunctions, and sex-dependent hippocampal pathophysiological mechanisms. This review synthesizes these findings in relation to the human PTSD phenomenology, argues for the necessity of developing genuinely translational animal models that capture individual variability and sex differences as key experimental variables, and discusses the methodological and ethical considerations surrounding the use of traumatic procedures in preclinical research.

title: Apoptotic body-liposome hybrid nanoparticles with photothermal-enhanced blood-brain barrier penetration for radiation-induced brain injury therapy.
abstract: Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) is a severe brain disease caused by cranial radiotherapy or accidental radiation exposure. RIBI causes overproduction of reactive oxygen species (ROS), resulting in oxidative injury to neurons and brain tissue and promoting neuroinflammation. Current treatments such as antioxidants, have limited efficacy due to limited penetration across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and rapid metabolic clearance. This study developed Prussian blue (PB) nanoparticles encapsulated in apoptotic body-hybrid liposomes to improve BBB penetration and ensure sustained antioxidative activity through controlled release of PB. PB serve as nanozymes for sustained ROS scavenging, while their photothermal response facilitates transient BBB modulation under near-infrared irradiation. Hybridization with apoptotic bodies provides a biomimetic membrane interface that supports cellular interactions and brain delivery. 2-Methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine (MPC)-modified DSPE-PEG2000 was incorporated through choline-related transport pathways for brain-targeted delivery. In vitro, PB@AbL showed approximately 55% DPPH radical-scavenging activity. In vivo, brain drug accumulation was increased by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS). Pharmacodynamic analysis showed reduced malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, increased glutathione (GSH) levels, improved neuronal survival, and cognitive function. This strategy offers a promising approach for the treatment of RIBI and other neurological disorders associated with oxidative stress.

title: Serrated polyp detection rates beyond adenoma detection rate for postcolonoscopy colorectal cancer: findings from the SCREESCO trial.
abstract: The association between serrated polyp detection rates, including proximal serrated polyp detection rate (PSPDR), and postcolonoscopy colorectal cancer (PCCRC) remains unestablished. We investigated PCCRC incidence and characteristics, and explored associations of PSPDR and adenoma detection rate (ADR) with PCCRC in colonoscopy- and fecal immunochemical test (FIT)-based screening within the Screening of Swedish Colons (SCREESCO) trial. Data from participants who underwent colonoscopy in the colonoscopy and FIT arms were analyzed. PCCRC, defined as colorectal cancer (CRC) diagnosed >6 months after a colonoscopy that did not detect CRC, was identified through linkage with cancer registries. Associations between PSPDR and PCCRC incidence were assessed using Cox models. Of 9982 and 5875 individuals in the colonoscopy and FIT arms, PCCRC was identified in 20 and 17 individuals, with 3-year PCCRC rates of 5.9% (3/51) and 3.5% (4/115), respectively. Compared with screening-detected CRC, PCCRC more often involved right-sided location and advanced stage. The 5-year cumulative incidence of PCCRC was 0.16% (95%CI 0.10%-0.27%) and 0.06% (95%CI 0.02%-0.15%) when colonoscopies were performed by endoscopists with low vs. high PSPDR (<10% vs. ≥10%), respectively. Among endoscopists with high ADR, 5-year PCCRC incidence was 0.13% (95%CI 0.04%-0.32%) vs. 0.06% (95%CI 0.02%-0.16%) for those with low vs. high PSPDR, respectively. Within this group, PCCRC incidence over 8 years decreased as PSPDR increased (hazard ratio per percentage-point increase, 0.90; 95%CI 0.82-1.00; P = 0.04). Despite the limited number of PCCRC events, this study suggests that PSPDR provides complementary information beyond ADR for identifying colonoscopies with higher PCCRC incidence.

title: Early-life high-fat diet accelerates the development of vagal satiation signaling and predisposes females to overconsumption.
abstract: Overconsumption of foods rich in fats, sugars, and calories is a major contributing factor to increased risk for cardiometabolic disease. Ingestive experience with these foods can begin early in children, yet there is limited understanding of the impact of early life nutrition on the development of vagal afferent neurons necessary for coordinating appetitive and satiating behaviors. To address this gap, mice reared on a chow diet (control) were compared to those reared on a high-fat diet (HFDEARLY). We demonstrate that the vagally mediated satiation response to cholecystokinin (CCK) does not mature until adolescence in chow-reared mice. However, HFDEARLY exposure triggers a precocious maturation of this response, accompanied by transcriptomic changes in the nodose ganglion. Durable changes in orosensory processing and appetitive behaviors are also evident in adult female HFDEARLY mice, which consume more lipid and calorie-dense liquid diet than controls, suggesting a lasting, sex-specific vulnerability to overconsumption of palatable, energy-dense foods.

title: Early caregiver mirroring predicts the emergence of action-unit-based facial representations in the infant brain.
abstract: Early caregiver-infant interactions play a crucial role in the development of facial expression understanding, but little is known about how early experience shapes the neural representation of facial expression information. In the adult brain, facial expressions are represented componentially, with neural activity encoding constituent facial muscle configurations, or action units (AUs), independently of global emotion categories. This may provide important functional advantages, but the developmental emergence of such a representational format is unclear. We examined whether neural representations of facial expressions become increasingly organised around AU structure across early development, and whether caregiver mirroring predicts this process. Electroencephalography (EEG) data were analysed from samples of nine-month-olds and 30-month-olds, who viewed short video clips of dynamic facial expressions. Nine-month-olds had also been observed during mother-infant interactions at two months of age. Time-resolved representational similarity analysis was used to characterise the dynamic geometry of neural representations. At 30 months, neural activity reliably encoded AU structure, whereas group-level AU encoding was not observed at nine months. However, individual differences in AU encoding at nine months were predicted by maternal mirroring of infant facial expressions at two months. This relationship was specific to direct mirroring responses, and was not explained by more general maternal responding. These findings suggest that neural representations of facial expressions become increasingly organised around constituent facial movements across early development, and that caregiver mirroring is associated with the emergence of componential facial representations. More generally, they provide initial evidence linking early embodied social interaction to the development of facial representational organisation.

title: Transorbital sonography reveals retrobulbar optic nerve neuroaxonal changes in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: The optic nerve (ON), as an extension of the central nervous system, reflects multiple sclerosis (MS) pathological processes. Transorbital sonography (TOS) is emerging as a novel technique to detect ON changes. Our aim was to investigate retrobulbar ON morphometric changes in MS and their relationship with prior history of optic neuritis. 122 MS subjects were enrolled, 68 with and 54 without history of optic neuritis. ON diameters without and with sheath were measured at 3 mm (OND3 and ONSD3) and 5 mm (ONSD5) posterior to the optic disc; myelination index (MI=ONSD3/ONSD5) was calculated. To account for intrasubject dependencies, linear mixed models (LMMs) for repeated measures were employed, adjusting for age at onset and body mass index. ONs with history of inflammation (I-ON) exhibited significantly reduced diameters versus companion nerves in both measurements with and without sheath (OND3: p = 0.002; ONSD3: p = 0.010; ONSD5: p = 0.046). All ONs diameters progressively decreased with increasing neuritis frequency, demonstrating a dose-response effect. Significant measurement reductions in OND and ONSD3 were observed in I-ON of patients with Expanded Disability Status Scale >3, whereas no significant differences emerged for progression index (PI) > 0.20 among ONs with and without history of optic neuritis. TOS reliably captures ON morphometric changes related to inflammatory history and chronic neuroaxonal injury in MS, supporting its role as a promising biomarker of disability burden and progression independent of relapse activity (PIRA).

title: Co-occurrence of myasthenia gravis and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder: A case series and literature review.
abstract: Patients with myasthenia gravis develop other autoimmune diseases in 5-30% of cases and have a higher incidence of demyelinating disorders than the general population. An increased risk of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder following thymectomy has also been reported. To describe two adult patients from Bogotá, Colombia, with concurrent myasthenia gravis and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder after thymectomy, and to provide a literature review. A retrospective literature review of articles published up to October 2024 was performed using PubMed and Embase with the terms "Neuromyelitis," "Thymectomy," "Myasthenia Gravis," and "Aquaporin 4." Studies in English or Spanish reporting myasthenia gravis and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder were included. Additionally, two adult patients from Bogotá who developed neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder after thymectomy for myasthenia gravis were analyzed. 60 patients were included, comprising 58 cases identified in the literature and 2 additional cases from our center. Two adult patients (one male, one female) previously diagnosed with myasthenia gravis developed neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder symptoms following thymectomy. The literature search yielded 24 articles describing 58 patients, 94.8% were women. Myasthenia gravis preceded neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder in most cases (85.7%). Thymectomy was reported in 39 of 58 patients (67.2%). Among patients in whom thymectomy preceded neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, the mean interval between thymectomy and NMOSD onset was 12.8 ± 9.3 years. Myasthenia gravis and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder coexistence follow a consistent pattern, supporting shared autoimmune susceptibility. Further studies are needed to clarify its clinical implications.

title: Editorial overview: Specifying cell identity, shaping tissue diversity.
Harnessing autophagy and its transcriptional regulation in tumorigenesis and neurodegeneration: Potential and existing therapeutic strategies.
abstract: Autophagy is a fundamental cellular process that maintains homeostasis by degrading and recycling cellular components. As autophagy is essential for metabolizing damaged organelles and toxic substances, it plays a crucial role in both normal physiology and pathological conditions. However, autophagy has dual roles in both tumorigenesis and neurodegeneration. In cancer, autophagy can act as a tumor suppressor by clearing damaged components in early stages, but promotes tumor survival and growth in later stages, particularly under stress. In neurodegeneration, impaired autophagy is implicated in the disease progression of conditions such as Alzheimer, Parkinson, and Huntington diseases, in which the failure to clear misfolded proteins and damaged organelles exacerbates disease pathology. This review is organized to cover the molecular machinery and transcriptional regulation of autophagy, its disease-specific subtypes, its dual roles in tumorigenesis and neurodegeneration, and the current pharmacological landscape for therapeutic targeting. Attention is given to pharmacological modulation of autophagy, including senolytic drugs that selectively eliminate senescent cells by exploiting their dependence on antiapoptotic survival pathways, and small-molecule regulators targeting key pathways such as phosphoinositide 3-kinase/Akt serine/threonine kinase/mechanistic target of rapamycin and AMP-activated protein kinase. Depending on the pathological context, these drugs are under development to either inhibit or induce autophagy. Additionally, we address the challenges and limitations in developing effective autophagy-targeting drugs, underscoring the need for further research to identify new compounds that can modulate cellular autophagic flux. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Autophagy is an important homeostatic mechanism, and its dysregulation contributes to a wide range of diseases, including cancer and neurodegenerative disorders. Therefore, a deeper mechanistic understanding of the regulation of autophagy is crucial for advancing targeted therapies with significant clinical impact.

title: Low-dose radiotherapy ameliorates Alzheimer's-like pathology in 5xFAD mice and is associated with HIF-1α-related inflammatory signaling downregulation.
abstract: Whether fractionated low-dose radiotherapy (LDRT) alleviates Alzheimer's disease-like pathology and whether these effects are associated with microglial HIF-1α-related signaling remain unclear. Male 5xFAD mice received whole-brain irradiation at 2 Gy per fraction for 5 fractions (total dose, 10 Gy). One month later, cognition was assessed by the Morris water maze and novel object recognition tests, and brain pathology was evaluated by immunofluorescence and Western blot. LPS-stimulated BV2 cells were used as an in vitro model to examine the effects of LDRT on nitric oxide, cytokines, and reactive oxygen species. Transcriptomic analysis was performed with 3 biological replicates per group, followed by pharmacological validation using the HIF-1α inhibitor YC-1. LDRT improved spatial and recognition memory, reduced Aβ plaque burden in the hippocampus and cortex, and attenuated microglial activation in 5xFAD mice. In particular, LDRT decreased the hippocampal Aβ plaque area fraction (P = 0.0065) and reduced HIF-1α expression in Iba1-positive microglia in the hippocampus (P = 0.0077). In addition, LDRT reduced Iba1 expression and CD68-positive area while preserving Aβ phagocytosis by primary microglia. In BV2 cells, LDRT inhibited LPS-induced inflammatory responses and altered 123 differentially expressed genes enriched in the HIF-1, IL-17, TNF, MAPK, and p53 signaling pathways. Pharmacological inhibition of HIF-1α by YC-1 recapitulated, but did not further enhance, the anti-inflammatory effects of LDRT. Fractionated whole-brain LDRT ameliorates cognitive deficits and Aβ pathology in 5xFAD mice, with effects associated with downregulation of microglial HIF-1α-related signaling.

title: Peripheral Nerve Blocks in the Treatment of Pediatric Headache and Neuralgia: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Pericranial peripheral nerve blocks are widely used in pediatric headache practice by subspecialty clinicians, but the published studies vary in technique, indications, and outcome reporting. The objective of this scoping review was to describe the existing evidence of pericranial peripheral nerve blocks for children and adolescents with primary and secondary headache disorders or cranial neuralgias. A systematic search was performed in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for scoping reviews. Searches were conducted in February 2025 and updated in February 2026. Study design, populations, indications, outcomes, and adverse events were summarized descriptively. No critical appraisal or meta-analysis was performed. The search identified 1503 records; after duplicate removal, full-text review, and bibliography searching, 39 studies were included (29 peer-reviewed articles and 10 abstracts) published between 1997 and 2025. The greater occipital nerve was the most frequently targeted. Chronic migraine and mixed primary headache were the most common indications. Lidocaine and bupivacaine were the most used anesthetics with steroids included in one-third of studies. Reported adverse events were typically mild and transient. No study reported serious procedure-related adverse events. Pediatric studies on pericranial nerve blocks for head pain span nearly three decades and consistently describe these procedures as safe and clinically helpful. However, literature is dominated by observational studies and case series, with few randomized controlled trials and variability in procedural techniques. Future collaborative pediatric research using standardized methodologies will help strengthen the evidence base and shape best practices for the care of head pain in youth.

title: Detergent-based preparation influences TMEM16F assembly and scramblase activity.
abstract: Transmembrane protein 16F (TMEM16F) is a Ca2+-dependent phospholipid scramblase that mediates phosphatidylserine externalization in various physiological processes, including blood coagulation. Although previous cryo-electron microscopy studies have established the homodimeric structure of TMEM16F and provided important structural insights, the mechanisms underlying substrate translocation and functional regulation remain incompletely understood. Here, we conducted a detailed in vitro analysis of TMEM16F using a reconstituted liposome system to elucidate its regulatory mechanisms. We found that the detergents used during protein purification strongly affect both the scramblase activity and the oligomeric state of TMEM16F. Specifically, proteoliposomes containing TMEM16F prepared with n-dodecyl-β-D-maltoside (DDM) exhibited faster scrambling kinetics and higher Ca2+ sensitivity than those prepared with other detergents. Unexpectedly, blue native gel electrophoresis revealed that the DDM-isolated TMEM16F contained additional higher-order assemblies, which was further supported by size-exclusion chromatography and atomic force microscopy. Collectively, these findings suggest that the preparation process with different detergents influences the oligomeric states and scramblase activities of TMEM16F. Our results suggest a potential link between the structural plasticity and function of TMEM16F and provide a critical framework for detergent choice in structural and functional studies of membrane protein complexes.

title: Interindividual variability of muscle involvement on imaging in a family with FLNC c.577G>A (p.A193T)-related myopathy.
abstract: FLNC-related myopathy (FLNC-RM) with actin-binding domain (ABD) variants is known to show heterogeneous muscle involvement; however, whether such variability exists within families sharing the same variant, and which muscles contribute to this heterogeneity, remain unclear. We investigated muscle involvement patterns in four members of a single family carrying the FLNC c.577G>A (p.A193T) variant who underwent serial longitudinal muscle imaging. A five-point semi-quantitative visual assessment of fatty replacement was performed across 43 muscles using whole-body CT and MRI, covering the shoulder, trunk, pelvis, thighs, and lower legs. Uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) provided a visualization in which longitudinal observations tended to group by individual. In the original 43-dimensional mMS matrix, the mean within-patient distance was smaller than the mean between-patient distance among P1a-c (3.58 vs. 7.29; exact permutation P = 0.00017), supporting the persistence of individual-specific mMS distribution profiles over the observed period. Analysis across muscles identified a subset-gluteus medius, gluteus minimus, adductor magnus, semimembranosus, gastrocnemius (medial and lateral heads), and soleus-for which mMS showed a strong fit to age-based models, while many other muscles showed marked interindividual variability. Chronological data further illustrated common and variable patterns of muscle involvement while preserving individual differences. Notably, relative preservation of the tibialis anterior and extensor digitorum longus was observed even at advanced stages. Overall, these findings indicate that FLNC-RM with the ABD variant, particularly the c.577G>A, is characterized by marked interindividual variability in muscle involvement patterns, even among members of the same family.

title: Language prediction in multimodal contexts: The contribution of iconic gestures to anticipatory sentence comprehension.
journal: Cortex; a journal devoted to the study of the nervous system and behavior
abstract: Evidence shows listeners predict upcoming words, and iconic gestures in face-to-face dialogue often precede their spoken referents. A recent framework proposes that early-onset gestures can pre-activate the meaning of upcoming nouns. This pre-registered EEG study tested this proposal. 81 Dutch adults watched videos of an actress producing discourses ending with a target noun. The noun was either predictable or not from the discourse. Each noun was paired with an iconic gesture whose stroke began either 520 msec (earlier) or 130 msec (later) before the noun. Discourse predictability produced the hypothesized post-target N400 reduction for predictable versus non-predictable items (H1). In the pre-target window, earlier gestures in non-predictable discourses elicited more negative amplitudes than in predictable discourses (H2a), suggesting that earlier gestures modulated neural responses when predictability was low. No comparable interaction was found for the opposite contrast (early-predictable vs late-predictable & late-non-predictable; H2c). In the post-target window, earlier gestures yielded a modest N400-like positivity relative to late gestures (H2e), but the interaction between gesture timing and discourse predictability (H2f) was not supported. A follow-up indicated that, in non-predictable discourses, later gestures produced a larger N400 than earlier gestures. Thus, the data confirm H1 and support H2a (and partially H2e), while H2c and H2f were not supported, suggesting that when speakers produce monologic discourses, earlier iconic gestures can aid anticipatory processing when linguistic predictions are weak, but their effect is limited and context-dependent. Together with the exploratory follow-up, the findings highlight a nuanced role of the influence of gesture timing on comprehension.

title: Reorienting TMS treatments for fear memories and posttraumatic stress disorder. The emerging potential of the anterior prefrontal cortex.
abstract: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is characterized by re-experiencing trauma through vivid and involuntary intrusions, avoidance of cues that could trigger traumatic memories, and alterations in mood and cognition. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) offers a promising approach to modulating activity and functional coupling within neural circuits underlying these processes. To date, TMS studies in fear-conditioning research and PTSD have mainly focused on dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) and ventromedial (vmPFC)-connected or broader medial-prefrontal (mPFC) targets, yielding encouraging but heterogeneous effects on posttraumatic symptoms. In parallel, emerging evidence has implicated the anterior prefrontal cortex (aPFC; Brodmann area 10) in threat- and trauma-related processes, including memory retrieval, higher-order control of defensive responding, adaptive strategy selection, and resilience. Whereas the dlPFC and vmPFC have been incorporated into mechanistic models of fear regulation, the aPFC has received limited attention in theoretical frameworks of fear and PTSD. Here, we review TMS studies organized around dlPFC, vmPFC-connected or mPFC, and aPFC neuroanatomical targets, integrating evidence from experimental and clinical research. Based on the hierarchical model of prefrontal organization, we argue that these regions represent potential TMS targets or circuit nodes, but likely act on partially distinct mechanisms. The vmPFC appears primarily involved in early automatic downregulation of defensive responses; the dlPFC may support cognitive control strategies such as reappraisal; and the aPFC may enable a supraordinate influence over higher-order representations and avoidance-related circuitry, as well as flexible selection of emotion-regulation strategies. We conclude that integrating the aPFC into this framework may guide next-generation, mechanistically-informed TMS treatments for PTSD.

title: The role of positive linguistic sentiment in extinction learning through exposure therapy.
abstract: Exposure therapy is derived from extinction learning principles. Evidence suggests that reward processes, including positive affect, may influence extinction learning. Few studies have explored the role of reward and positive affect in exposure. This study sought to address gaps by examining whether linguistic markers of positive affect expressed during exposure predicted learning and clinical outcomes. Adults (N = 47) with social anxiety or panic disorder completed nine sessions of exposure therapy. Participants rated expected likelihood of feared outcome occurrence before and after each exposure, and the difference (expectancy change) was calculated as a measure of learning. Natural language processing was used to analyze sentiment in written and spoken language during consolidation of extinction learning immediately after exposure, resulting in a score that reflected tendency towards positive over negative affect. Anxiety symptoms were assessed weekly at each exposure session and at end of treatment. Higher positive sentiment was associated with greater expectancy change at the between-person level for written and within-person level for spoken sentiment. Higher within-person positive sentiment predicted lower next-session anxiety for spoken sentiment only. Sentiment did not predict overall clinical outcomes. This is the first study to test the role of linguistic sentiment in exposure learning mechanisms and outcomes. More positive sentiment during exposure consolidation may support greater learning and reduced next-session symptoms, but may be insufficient in affecting overall clinical outcomes. It is possible that exposure learning may be maximized by directing attention towards more positive exposure elements; further study is needed to test this.

title: Treg-associated oligomannose N-glycans trigger immune dysregulation in myasthenia gravis.
abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is an autoimmune neurological disease driven by the production of autoantibodies against components of the neuromuscular junction, resulting in fatigable muscle weakness, and in more severe cases, leading to life-threatening complications. This breakdown of immune tolerance has been associated with an impaired suppressive function and altered frequency of Regulatory T cells (Tregs) in autoimmune diseases, including MG. As key regulators of immune tolerance, Tregs play a pivotal role in maintaining immune homeostasis through their ability to suppress other immune cells, controlling inflammation. Nevertheless, the mechanisms underlying Tregs dysfunction in MG pathogenesis are not fully understood. Here, we reveal the impact of Treg N-glycosylation on their immunoregulatory activity and function in the MG context. Glycan profiling by flow cytometry of circulating Tregs from MG patients (n = 72) and healthy controls (HCs; n = 24) revealed increased presence of oligomannose N-glycans in disease. Moreover, this specific Treg N-glycome profile was associated with disease severity, distinguishing between active disease and remission, being more pronounced in MG patients with additional autoimmune diseases, highlighting its potential as a disease biomarker. Functionally, in vitro abrogation of the N-glycosylation pathway in Tregs (mimicking the oligomannose enrichment found in the patients) resulted in impaired suppressive capacity over conventional T cells. Consistently, in the Experimental Autoimmune Myasthenia Gravis (EAMG) model, mice with altered Treg N-glycosylation exhibited worse clinical features and a reduced frequency of effector Tregs compared to wild-type controls. Altogether, these findings identify N-glycosylation as a mechanism underlying Treg dysfunction in MG, in which abnormal expression of mannose-enriched N-glycans in Tregs associates with compromised Treg suppressive function and increased disease severity, proposing Treg N-glycosylation as both a mechanistic driver of MG pathogenesis and a potential avenue for therapeutic intervention.

title: Beyond primary motor cortex: clinical relevance of non-primary motor areas in upper-extremity recovery after stroke-A scoping review.
journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
abstract: Facilitating excitability of the ipsilesional primary motor cortex can help enhance upper-extremity recovery in individuals with mild motor impairments after stroke. However, results are mixed in those with moderate-to-severe motor impairments. Extensive damage to the ipsilesional primary motor cortex may require non-primary motor areas and the contralesional primary motor cortex to assume aspects of ipsilesional primary motor cortex function. Nonetheless, the role of these areas in upper-extremity recovery is unclear. Thus, this scoping review comprehensively summarized evidence on the roles of non-primary and primary motor areas in upper-extremity muscle recovery after moderate-to-severe stroke. Eleven studies met the inclusion criteria. Findings varied by corticospinal tract integrity and time since stroke. Individuals with greater corticospinal tract integrity relied primarily on ipsilesional primary motor cortex for proximal and distal muscle recovery. With greater corticospinal tract damage, recovery increasingly relied on non-primary motor areas. Proximal muscle recovery involved the contralesional dorsal premotor cortex, whereas distal recovery involved a broader network including premotor cortices, supplementary motor area, cingulate motor area, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, and intraparietal sulcus. During the acute and subacute phases, the contralesional intraparietal sulcus showed maladaptive effects, whereas in the chronic phase, the contralesional dorsal premotor cortex supported recovery. Future trials should investigate the contributions of the contralesional intraparietal sulcus and ipsilesional and contralesional dorsal premotor cortices across recovery phases after moderate-to-severe stroke. Registration doi: 10.17605/OSF.IO/YH7E6.

title: Evolution of daytime PaCO2 in patients with neuromuscular disorders and OSA using CPAP: a retrospective study.
abstract: Neuromuscular disorders (NMD) are frequently complicated by obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), which may add an obstructive ventilatory load and contribute to CO2 retention. While non-invasive ventilation (NIV) is recommended for established hypoventilation, the impact of continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) on daytime PaCO2 in NMD remains poorly documented. We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study in a tertiary neuromuscular referral center. Consecutive adults with NMD undergoing respiratory assessment were included if they had (i) OSA treated with CPAP and (ii) daytime PaCO2 measurements before and after CPAP initiation. The primary outcome was paired PaCO2 change. Prespecified analyses were performed in patients with baseline PaCO2 ≥42 and ≥ 45 mmHg. Predictors of PaCO2 decrease were explored using logistic regression. One hundred patients were included, median AHI was 36.9/h. At a median follow-up of 13.6 months, PaCO2 decreased from 42.0 [39.0-44.0] to 40.5 [38.3-43.0] mmHg, corresponding to a paired reduction of 1.0 mmHg (95%CI 0.3-2.0; p = 0.01). PaCO2 decreased in 61% of patients, remained unchanged in 9%, and increased in 30%. In patients with baseline PaCO2≥45 mmHg (n = 18), the median PaCO2 reduction was 1.3 mmHg (95%CI 0.25-2.5; p = 0.016) and 8 patients normalized their PaCO2 but 4 experienced a deterioration. Baseline PaCO2 was the only independent predictor of PaCO2 decrease. In NMD patients with OSA, CPAP was associated with a modest but significant reduction in daytime PaCO2. Responses were heterogeneous, supporting careful patient phenotyping and structured reassessment after CPAP initiation to avoid delayed NIV escalation in non-responders.

title: Machine learning based identification of anxiety disorders using autonomic biomarkers: a diagnostic cross-validation study.
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the validity and reliability of autonomic biomarkers derived from heart rate variability (HRV) to correctly classify cases with and without anxiety disorder symptoms. This multi-center diagnostic cross-validation study involved 124 participants at two research labs, Sussex and Sheffield. Participants were exposed to a three-phase anxiety induction paradigm lasting 9 minutes (3 min. rest, 3 min. induction, 3 min. recovery). Participants completed measures of anxiety (GAD-7) and depression (PHQ-9) prior to the lab task. Their HRV was measured continuously using: [1] an industry-standard electrocardiogram (ECG) and [2] a miniaturized photoplethysmography (PPG) biosensor. Correlations between [1] and [2] were examined. A machine learning classifier was developed using ECG and PPG-derived features in a training sample from Sussex (n = 88) to identify cases with anxiety disorders (GAD-7 ≥ 8). Classification accuracy was evaluated using the area-under-the-curve (AUC) in the validation sample from Sheffield (n = 36). Correlations using dimensional scores were used to evaluate the machine learning model's convergent (GAD-7) and discriminant validity (PHQ-9). HRV features from PPG and ECG were strongly correlated across all three phases (r ≥ .88, p < .001). An ECG-based machine learning classifier generalized to an external validation sample (AUC= .71), correctly classifying anxiety disorder cases with adequate sensitivity (88%) and specificity (61%) and outperforming a PPG-based classifier. As expected, the classifier had marginally higher correlations with GAD-7 (r= .51) than PHQ-9 (r= .47). Biomarker data processed using a machine learning algorithm converges with an established measure of anxiety. This supports the potential use of HRV-derived biomarkers to monitor changes in real-time, which could be highly informative for exposure-based therapies.

title: Exploring the neuroprotective potential of saponins through the gut microbiota-brain axis: a narrative review of emerging mechanisms and research directions.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are defined as progressive and irreversible disorders involving the degeneration of neurons in the brain, giving rise to both cognitive deterioration and motor dysfunction. Diseases such as Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and Huntington's pose major public health challenges, particularly in aging populations, and are driven by complex mechanisms including oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and abnormal protein aggregation. Recent evidence suggests that alterations in gut microbiota composition are closely linked to the onset and progression of these disorders. Saponins have been reported to modulate gut microbiota composition and preclinical studies indicate that certain saponins may exert neuroprotective actions in specific models of neurodegeneration. This review summarizes and interprets the emerging, preliminary role of saponins in modulating pathways implicated in neurodegeneration, with a particular focus on their capacity to influence the gut microbiota-brain axis. Specifically, we summarize scientific evidence on how the structural features of saponins shape gut microbial composition and activity, thereby influencing their potential to modulate the development and progression of neurodegenerative disorders. Microbial metabolites, neuroinflammatory cascades, and redox balance represent key pathways potentially influenced by saponins in preclinical contexts, 2 central drivers of neurodegenerative progression. This review also highlights the preliminary nature of current evidence on these potential mechanisms and discusses major knowledge gaps, including saponin toxicity and the need for clinical studies before meaningful translation.

title: A tunable brain-targeted PEGylated ginsenoside Rg1 derivative disrupts the ROS-mediated inflammasome-pyroptosis cascade to ameliorate Alzheimer's cognitive deficits.
abstract: The pathogenic cascade of oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and pyroptosis serves as a core driving factor in the pathogenesis and progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Although ginsenoside Rg1 exhibits pleiotropic neuroprotective activities, its poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability severely hinders its clinical translation. To overcome this limitation, a brain-targeted delivery system was constructed using a covalent conjugation strategy, linking purified Rg1 with rhodamine B-modified polyethylene glycol (PEG) of varying chain lengths (Rg1s-PEG). After screening, the derivative Rg1s-PEG-600 was identified as achieving an optimal balance between hydrophilic stealth properties and steric hindrance, demonstrating enhanced brain accumulation and favorable biosafety profiles. In both in vitro and in vivo models of lipopolysaccharide-induced acute neuroinflammation, Rg1s-PEG-600 attenuated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, inhibited canonical neuronal pyroptosis mediated by the NLRP1/3 inflammasomes, and significantly ameliorated behavioral deficits and synaptic loss. Furthermore, in chronic 5xFAD transgenic mice, systemic administration of Rg1s-PEG-600 for 12 weeks markedly reversed spatial memory decline, anxiety-like behavior, and synaptic protein depletion. Mechanistic studies further revealed that this targeted nanotherapeutic not only suppressed the ROS-NLRP1 signaling axis and subsequent neuronal pyroptosis in the AD brain but also comprehensively inhibited amyloidogenesis and Tau hyperphosphorylation. This work provides a promising, multitarget nanotherapeutic strategy to overcome BBB limitations and disrupt the complex pathological networks underlying neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Implanted and degradable hydrogel evaporative cooler for regional and repeated mild hypothermia therapy of traumatic brain injury.
abstract: Implantable, regional and repeated mild hypothermia represents a promising therapeutic strategy for traumatic brain injury. Here, we develop a soft, degradable hydrogel microchannel evaporative cooler capable of removing heat through water evaporation in microchannels and achieving focused regional cooling within a short time. Fabricated from degradable hydrogels and using water as the coolant, the cooler shows biocompatibility and tissue adhesion. In vivo intracranial experiments with the cooler adhered on the rat dura mater enabled precise temperature regulation during repeated regional hypothermia (33 ± 0.5 °C, 4 h per day for 3 consecutive days). The treatment conferred neuroprotection and supported neural repair, with therapeutic effects persisting for 14 days. Sustained recovery was associated with increased Nestin+/Ki67+ and Sox2+/Ki67+ cells, along with elevated MAP2/PSD95 co-localization. Additional staining confirmed the presence of Nestin+/GFAP- and Sox2+/GFAP- cell populations, supporting the involvement of progenitor-like cells. At 28 days post-injury, rats receiving treatment exhibited reduced lesion volume, preserved axonal integrity and myelination, and ameliorated cognitive performance. Proteomic profiling performed at day 3 further suggested that repeated hypothermia modulates synaptic plasticity, dampens neuroinflammation, and rescues perturbed energy metabolism, representing a multi-faceted response distinct from single-episode hypothermia. Collectively, these findings highlight the translational potential of this implantable cooling strategy for TBI therapy.

title: GM1 oligosaccharide reprograms Neuro2a-derived extracellular vesicles for selective, low-disruption membrane interactions.
abstract: The GM1 oligosaccharide β-Gal-(1-3)-β-GalNAc-(1-4)-[α-Neu5Ac-(2-3)]-β-Gal-(1-4)-Glc (OligoGM1) represents the soluble, bioactive portion of GM1 ganglioside and recapitulates many of its trophic, protective, and restorative effects. Our previous proteomic studies on OligoGM1-treated neuroblastoma cells revealed alterations in endocytic trafficking and extracellular vesicles (EVs) biogenesis suggesting a potential role for OligoGM1 in modulating EV biogenesis. Here, we apply a multi-technique biophysical platform to investigate the physico-chemical properties and functionality of EVs released by murine neuroblastoma Neuro2a cells, treated with OligoGM1. We show that OligoGM1 treatment slightly shifts to lower values the EVs' size population distribution and increases their relative lipid content, accompanied by a higher proportion of membrane-associated proteins. Our analysis further indicates that OligoGM1-treated cells release EVs with altered bilayer structural parameters, including increased apparent membrane thickness, consistent with a modified distribution of lipid/protein contributions within the adopted membrane model. Functional characterization using biomimetic model membranes indicates that EVs from treated and untreated cells differ in protein insertion and lipid exchange efficiency, pointing to distinct membrane-interaction modes relevant to downstream cellular interactions. Overall, these findings suggest that OligoGM1 reshapes the molecular architecture and biophysical behaviour of Neuro2a-derived EVs, providing membrane-level fingerprints that may be relevant for future studies of EV-cell interactions in neurodegenerative models.

title: Predicting cognitive-behavioral therapy outcomes in obsessive-compulsive disorder from inhibitory control neural activity: A mega-analysis and machine learning study from the ENIGMA-OCD consortium.
journal: European neuropsychopharmacology : the journal of the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology
abstract: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is an effective treatment for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), yet it remains difficult to predict who will respond. This study investigates associations between neural activity during inhibitory control tasks and CBT outcomes, and its value as a predictive marker of CBT outcome. Using fMRI data from individuals performing an inhibitory control task across five ENIGMA-OCD samples (n = 130, age range=8-57, 54% female), mass-univariate associations were analyzed between response inhibition and error processing activity and three CBT outcomes: response, remission, and change in symptom severity. Random forest classifier and support vector machine models using leave-one-sample-out and 5-fold cross-validation were used to predict CBT response and remission from fMRI activity and clinical data. Remission after CBT was associated with weaker activity in default mode regions during response inhibition and in the right supramarginal gyrus during error processing. Greater symptom reduction was linked to weaker pre-treatment activity across frontoparietal, dorsal attention, visual, and subcortical regions during response inhibition, and stronger default mode activity during error processing. These group-level effects were partially confirmed with machine learning, which predicted CBT response using inhibitory and error-related activity with modest AUC values of 0.66-0.67. Prediction of CBT remission or using other data types did not exceed chance-level. Wide-spread weaker activity during response inhibition and stronger activity in default mode regions during error processing pre-treatment appear beneficial for CBT. Despite modestly predictive AUC-values, these findings cannot yet be translated into clinically relevant individual markers of CBT outcome.

title: To smoke or not to smoke: smoking among people with depression or bipolar disorder.
journal: European neuropsychopharmacology : the journal of the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology

title: Effects of visual remediation on contour integration performance in schizophrenia spectrum disorders.
abstract: Impairments in visual processing, including difficulties in perceptual organization, are well documented in schizophrenia and related serious mental illnesses. These impairments are thought to contribute to reductions in higher-order cognition and functioning. The present study examined whether a visual remediation intervention targeting low- and mid-level visual processing improves perceptual organization in this population. Participants with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder were randomized to visual remediation (VR) or an active control (AC) condition.
