title: Spontaneous spiking in photoreceptors of Periplaneta americana.
journal: Journal of comparative physiology. A, Neuroethology, sensory, neural, and behavioral physiology
abstract: Insect photoreceptors are non-spiking neurons that encode visual information with graded voltage responses produced by stochastic activation of the phototransduction cascade in the microvilli. However, light-evoked, voltage-gated sodium channel (NaV) dependent axonal spikes have been reported in several species, where they are thought to support downstream signal transmission. Here we report a new mode of electrical activity in rhabdomeric photoreceptors: spontaneous trains of small, fast spikes appearing in darkness immediately after piercing the membrane. These spike trains differed from both quantum bumps and conventional axonal spikes. They occurred without light stimulation, persisted for tens of seconds to minutes, exhibited several millivolt amplitudes, and had kinetics and waveforms resembling NaV-dependent regenerative action potentials. Several lines of evidence indicated that spikes are generated in distal parts of the axon. First, spiking was suppressed by off-axis illumination that produced minimal somatic hyperpolarization, consistent with the effects of lateral interactions on axon terminals in the neuropil. Second, observation of spike superposition indicated that they can arise from multiple electrotonically separated loci and summate at the soma, suggesting distal, spatially separated spike-generating sites. Third, while spiking was sensitive to experimentally imposed changes in somatic membrane potential, spike frequency and duration often changed spontaneously and independently of it. Spiking spontaneously and irreversibly terminated through a gradual decline in spike frequency and often amplitude, consistent with a progressive reduction in NaV channel availability. Our results suggest that spontaneous spike trains reflect a transient shift in axonal excitability, possibly triggered by electrical perturbations associated with membrane penetration.

title: Constructing melanopic light exposure profiles from sparse daily-route measurements.
abstract: Daily light exposure is temporally structured, yet calibrated spectral measurements are usually available only at selected locations and times. Turning such a sparse library into a schedule-resolved profile requires an assignment rule: a decision about which measurements may represent each unmeasured part of the day. We examined how much that decision matters. Sixty-three eye-level spectral irradiance measurements, collected across home, commute, office and lunch settings on three June days in Ottawa, were mapped onto a schedule of 22 half-hour slots. For each of six assignment rules we generated 100,000 profiles and computed melanopic dose and time above thresholds of 250, 1,000 and 10,000 melanopic lx. Indoor-only and outdoor-only assignments gave contrasting bounds, with median doses of 16,536 and 119,995 lx ⋅ h. Among the four rules that combined indoor and outdoor measurements, median dose varied only from 44,257 to 48,337 lx ⋅ h, whereas the central 95% of the generated dose distributions spanned ranges differing by nearly a factor of two. Central estimates were set largely by the composition of the eligible measurement pools rather than by the structure a rule preserved; the rule mainly determined spread. Targeted substitutions, in which only commute and lunch conditions were changed, raised median dose by 28,600 lx ⋅ h, with outdoor lunch contributing more cumulative dose and outdoor commuting more time above 10,000 lx. The framework supports sensitivity and scenario analysis rather than reconstruction of continuous personal exposure, and shows why the assignment step must be reported explicitly for a constructed profile to be interpretable.

title: Immune-related gene expression links anxiety, depression, and pain outcomes in adolescence.
abstract: Chronic pain and internalising disorders such as anxiety and depression frequently co-occur during adolescence. Although prospective associations between internalising symptoms and later pain have been reported previously, the biological mechanisms underlying individual differences in this relationship remain poorly understood. Immune- and oxidative stress-related pathways, including the NRF2 gene, may contribute to such variability. This study investigated whether polymorphisms in the NRF2 gene (rs6721961 and rs35652124) are related to the association between anxiety and depression symptoms at age 14-15 and pain complaints two years later at age 16-17. Data were drawn from the IMAGEN longitudinal study (N = 724). Anxiety and depression symptoms were assessed using the Development and Well-Being Assessment (DAWBA), and pain complaints were measured via the Children's Somatization Inventory (CSI). Genotyping was conducted for NRF2 SNPs rs6721961 and rs35652124. Regression analyses tested main effects, followed by genotype-stratified analyses. Consistent with previous literature, higher levels of anxiety and depression at age 14-15 predicted increased pain complaints at age 16-17. Carriers of the TG/TT genotype of rs6721961 had significantly lower anxiety scores and reported fewer pain complaints compared to those carrying the GG genotype of rs6721961. Notably, the association between anxiety and later pain was significant only among individuals with the GG genotype. While replicating established associations between adolescent early internalising symptoms and later pain, this study suggests that genetic variation in NRF2 is related to the anxiety-pain association. Specifically, rs6721961 is associated with differences in susceptibility to pain among adolescents with elevated anxiety symptoms.

title: French psychiatric caregivers' perceptions of psychedelics: A national survey.
abstract: The use of psychedelic substances such as LSD, psilocybin, and dimethyltryptamine is currently being re-evaluated for their therapeutic potential in psychiatry. While international clinical research had started in the 2010s, France only initiated its first psychedelic trials in 2024. This study aimed to explore the knowledge, perceptions, and attitudes of French mental health professionals regarding the use of psychedelics in clinical and recreational settings. An anonymous online survey was conducted between December 2023 and January 2024 among psychiatry caregivers in France. The questionnaire included 19 items across five sections: demographic information, knowledge of psychedelics, perception of their therapeutic and recreational use, and personal experimentation with psychoactive substances. Data was analyzed using linear and ordinal regressions, controlling for age, gender, profession and experience with ketamine. A total of 298 respondents participated, primarily from public hospitals. Most were psychiatrists (41.4%) or psychologists (20.4%). About 88% had heard of medical studies on psychedelics, with high awareness of psilocybin and ketamine use in treatment-resistant depression. However, awareness of other therapeutic indications was limited. Fifty-three percent rated the therapeutic benefit-risk ratio of psychedelics as favorable, whereas 61% rated recreational use as dangerous. Favorable perception of therapeutic use was associated with male gender, personal experience with psychedelics, and clinical practice with ketamine. However, in a subgroup of clinicians (psychiatrists, residents, nurses) only clinical practice with ketamine remained significantly associated with favorable opinions. Personal experimentation was the only predictor of more positive attitudes toward recreational use. The results indicated a moderate but cautious openness among French psychiatry caregivers towards therapeutic psychedelics, less enthusiastic than in other international surveys. Their opinions were strongly influenced by personal and clinical experience. A notable finding was the clear separation caregivers made between therapeutic and recreational contexts. French psychiatry caregivers are aware of the growing interest in psychedelics and express moderate support for their medical use. Clinical practice with ketamine appears to play a pivotal role in shaping favorable attitudes. As France embarks on clinical trials with psychedelics, caregiver perspectives are likely to evolve, warranting further surveys in the coming years.

title: Father engagement in child and adolescent mental health care: From neurobiology to clinical practice.
journal: Current problems in pediatric and adolescent health care
abstract: Fathers influence child development through biological, relational, and family-system pathways, yet they remain comparatively underrepresented in research and child mental health care. Emerging neurobiological evidence suggests that paternal caregiving is associated with experience-dependent adaptations in neural and neuroendocrine systems involved in caregiving and social responsiveness. Developmental research further identifies both direct pathways, including father-child interaction, play, caregiving, and emotional responsiveness, and indirect pathways involving coparenting, family functioning, resources, and support of other caregivers. These processes may also influence children's emotional and behavioral health, although much of the evidence is observational and should not be interpreted as establishing causality. Despite the importance of fathers within children's developmental environments, fathers remain underrepresented in parenting intervention research and may be insufficiently engaged in psychiatric assessment and treatment. Father-inclusive care requires moving beyond physical presence or appointment attendance toward meaningful participation in assessment, treatment planning, behavioral interventions, medication monitoring, and safety planning when clinically appropriate. National, state, and health-system initiatives provide models for improving father engagement. This review proposes a practical framework: Identify, Invite, Listen, Engage, Collaborate, and Sustain, for incorporating fathers and father figures into child and adolescent mental health care while recognizing diverse family structures, safety considerations, and individual circumstances.

title: Bispectral index-suppression ratio discordance during general anaesthesia.
The Sound of Hypnotherapy: Identification of Paralinguistic Speech Features Using Acoustic Analysis and Deep Learning.
journal: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
abstract: Hypnosis is an altered state of consciousness characterized by focused attention and heightened suggestibility, with therapeutic applications in a range of mental and somatic conditions. While prior research has emphasized the linguistic content of hypnotic suggestions (ie, what is said), the paralinguistic and acoustic characteristics of the hypnotist's speech (ie, how it is said) remain underexplored. This study investigated condition-associated paralinguistic characteristics in recordings of 32 hypnotherapists across hypnosis and control conditions, during both reading and spontaneous tasks. We first applied classical acoustic analysis using Praat to examine common temporal, energy, frequency, and spectral parameters of connected speech on the entire recordings. The findings identify a paralinguistic profile within this sample characterized by a lower proportion of voicing, reduced intensity, and decreased spectral energy at low frequencies in the hypnosis condition. We then employed deep learning techniques, training classifiers on both handcrafted acoustic features and mel spectrograms. Within the present dataset and for therapists represented during training, the models reliably distinguished 12-second speech segments from hypnosis and control conditions, with fundamental frequency and formant-related features (F0 and F1-F3) emerging as key predictors. Spectrogram-based models achieved higher performance, suggesting that additional acoustic cues contribute to classification under the present recording protocol.

title: Remembered event features shape default mode network engagement during emotional memory recall.
abstract: Episodic memory involves reconstruction of past events through integration of multiple types of information, including perceptual details, narrative content, and emotional tone. The default mode network (DMN) is a set of regions thought to support episodic retrieval, yet it remains unclear how distinct subnetworks contribute to recall of these different memory features. Here, we examined how DMN subnetworks support and represent memory for naturalistic emotional events. Male and female human participants encoded short news videos that varied in emotional valence and recalled them in response to neutral cues during functional MRI scanning. Videos were again recalled one day later and memories were scored for perceptual and narrative details. Activity in the dorsomedial subnetwork was related to the emotional valence of the memory, while activity in the medial temporal subnetwork was associated with the number of perceptual details recalled. Multivariate pattern analyses further revealed that the medial temporal subnetwork exhibited greater pattern stability across recalls when recalling more perceptual details, while stability in the dorsomedial and core subnetworks was tied to emotional remembering. Our findings suggest that the dorsomedial subnetwork provides an affective frame for a memory, while the medial temporal subnetwork contributes perceptual specificity. These results demonstrate that the contents of memory retrieval shape network engagement during emotional recall, providing insight into how the brain reconstructs complex real-world experiences.Significance Statement How do we remember the emotional tone of an event versus its visual details? This study examines how distinct subnetworks within the brain's default mode network (DMN) contribute to remembering different features of memory. While the medial temporal subnetwork is connected to retrieving the perceptual details of past events, the dorsomedial subnetwork supports recall of the emotional tone. Furthermore, patterns of activity in the medial temporal subnetwork are more stable when recalling more perceptually rich memories, while stability in the dorsomedial subnetwork is tied to emotional remembering. These findings suggest that the default mode network flexibly responds to different kinds of memory features, supporting the reconstruction of rich emotional memories from complex real-world experiences.

title: Acute intermittent porphyria: abdominal pain, weight loss and acute neuropathy.
A wearable nanofluidic sensor for determining the sweat nicotine.
abstract: The escalating prevalence of electronic cigarettes has intensified public health discourse regarding the implications of nicotine exposure. Consequently, the development of rigorous, non-invasive diagnostic methodologies to evaluate secondhand smoke exposure is imperative. Precise quantification of nicotine levels provides a critical evidence base for designing interventions aimed at smoking cessation and the prophylaxis of smoking-related pathologies. In this study, we introduce a novel biosensing paradigm that leverages the I-V characteristics of asymmetric nanochannel arrays, synergized with the selective enzymatic activity of nicotine oxidase (CYP2B6), for the detection of sweat nicotine. The nanoconfinement effect within these arrays significantly enhances the affinity of CYP2B6 for nicotine, thereby augmenting catalytic efficiency. The developed wearable sensor demonstrates exceptional analytical performance, featuring a bilinear range (0.1 to 9 μM and 10-50 μM) and robust immunity to common sweat-borne interferences, such as glucose and uric acid. Furthermore, the platform exhibits a low limit of detection (0.3 μM) at low nicotine concentration range, underscoring its clinical utility for the sensitive quantification of nicotine exposure. We assessed nicotine levels in human populations, including high smokers, low smokers, secondhand smokers, and non-smokers. The results indicated that a clear increase in nicotine levels correlating with the duration of smoking. Thus, the continuous and personalized wearable sweat nicotine detection sensor based on the proposed detection method can effectively monitor nicotine exposure across a diverse range of populations.

title: A blood-brain barrier-penetrating NIR fluorescent probe enables cross-model optical imaging of H2O2 in three neuroinflammation-related experimental mice models of brain injury.
abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is a key mediator of oxidative stress in neuroinflammation-related brain injury, yet brain H2O2 imaging remains challenging because of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and tissue autofluorescence. In addition, most reported probes have been evaluated in only one or a few disease models, limiting cross-model comparison. Here, we developed MH-1, an H2O2-responsive near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent probe for brain-section optical mapping after systemic administration. MH-1 exhibited an approximately 60-fold fluorescence turn-on at 667 nm, enabled H2O2 detection over 0.107-1000 μmol/L, and reached a stable response within approximately 30 min, with high selectivity, interference resistance, pH stability, and low cytotoxicity. Its fluorescence quantum yield increased from 0.72% to 2.45% upon activation. CD31 co-staining confirmed MH-1-associated fluorescence in extravascular brain parenchyma after systemic administration. Ex vivo brain-section imaging further revealed model-dependent H2O2-associated fluorescence in LPS-induced neonatal neuroinflammation, hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE), and Alzheimer's disease (AD), with an effective imaging window of approximately 12 h. Rather than relying on a single best-in-class analytical parameter, MH-1 integrates NIR emission, a large fluorescence turn-on, BBB access, and applicability across three mechanistically distinct brain-injury models. This combined performance enables region-resolved, cross-model comparison of H2O2-associated oxidative stress in preclinical brain tissue.
